question: In a vector-projection investigation, a measured vector is $\vec{a}=4\hat{i}-3\hat{j}+12\hat{k}$, while the direction of a reference line is represented by $\vec{b}=2\hat{i}+2\hat{j}+\hat{k}$. Students analyse how much of $\vec{a}$ acts along the reference direction. They first calculate the component-based scalar product and the angle between the vectors, and then use the scalar product to obtain both the scalar and vector projections of $\vec{a}$ on $\vec{b}$.(a) Calculate $|\vec{a}|$ and $|\vec{b}|$.(b) Evaluate $\vec{a}\cdot\vec{b}$.(c) Determine the angle between $\vec{a}$ and $\vec{b}$.(d) Find the scalar projection and vector projection of $\vec{a}$ on $\vec{b}$.
explanation: (a)`|\vec{a}|=\sqrt{4^2+(-3)^2+12^2}|\vec{a}|=\sqrt{16+9+144}=13`Also,`|\vec{b}|=\sqrt{2^2+2^2+1^2}=3`(b)Using corresponding components,`\vec{a}\cdot\vec{b}=(4)(2)+(-3)(2)+(12)(1)\vec{a}\cdot\vec{b}=8-6+12=14`(c)If $\theta$ is the angle between the vectors, then`\cos\theta=\frac{\vec{a}\cdot\vec{b}}{|\vec{a}||\vec{b}|}\cos\theta=\frac{14}{(13)(3)}=\frac{14}{39}`Therefore,`\theta=\cos^{-1}\left(\frac{14}{39}\right)`(d)The scalar projection of $\vec{a}$ on $\vec{b}$ is`\frac{\vec{a}\cdot\vec{b}}{|\vec{b}|}=\frac{14}{3}`The vector projection is`\operatorname{proj}_{\vec{b}}\vec{a}=\frac{\vec{a}\cdot\vec{b}}{|\vec{b}|^2}\vec{b}\operatorname{proj}_{\vec{b}}\vec{a}=\frac{14}{9}(2\hat{i}+2\hat{j}+\hat{k})\operatorname{proj}_{\vec{b}}\vec{a}=\frac{28}{9}\hat{i}+\frac{28}{9}\hat{j}+\frac{14}{9}\hat{k}`
